entries.title: Proverbs 28:1
segments: Guilt is timorous, and innocence bold.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:2
segments:
For; because of. 
 
  Many are the princes thereof; it is continually changing rulers, as we see illustrated in the history of Israel after the revolt of the ten tribes: which is a sore calamity to a nation. 
 
God punishes wicked and corrupt nations by giving them up to frequent and violent changes of government, with all the confusion and misery that follow in their train.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:3
segments: A poor man; in eastern countries avaricious men, destitute alike of property and principle, often obtain the government of provinces, which they plunder at pleasure.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:4
segments: Wicked men are naturally inclined to take part with those who are, like themselves, against the righteous.  Hence there must be a perpetual conflict between the two classes.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:8
segments: For him that will pity the poor; God will take it from him, and give it to him that will pity the poor.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:10
segments:
Causeth the righteous to go astray; seeks to lead him astray. 
 
  The upright; whom he sought to mislead.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:11
segments: Searcheth him out; finds out his folly.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:12
segments:
Great glory; the state is prosperous and honored. 
 
  A man is hidden; a good man is driven into obscurity. 
 
Upright rulers are the glory and strength of a nation; and wicked men its shame and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:13
segments: There is but one way to escape the ruinous consequences of sin, which is by confessing and forsaking it.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:14
segments:
Feareth; God. 
 
  Hardeneth his heart; against God's authority.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:16
segments:
A great oppressor; it is implied that he shall also come to a violent end. 
 
The highest wisdom of a prince is to seek the welfare of the people committed to his care, for in their prosperity lie his own quiet and security.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:17
segments:
Doeth violence to the blood of any person; is laden with the guilt of shedding human blood. 
 
  Shall flee to the pit; shall go down speedily to the dead. 
 
  Stay him; prevent his going to the pit. 
 
That the murderer shall die, is a divine ordinance.  All who seek to set it aside, oppose themselves alike to the wisdom of God and the welfare of the community.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:21
segments: The elevation of selfish and unprincipled men to ofice is a great public calamity; they will pervert justice and sacrifice the highest interests of the people for private emolument.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:22
segments:
Hasteth to be rich; is greedy of gain, and uses unlawful means to procure it. 
 
The avaricious man, who scruples not to use unjust means for the increase of his estate, is on the highway to final poverty and ruin.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:23
segments: Honest dealing with offenders is the way to secure their respect.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:26
segments:
Wisely; with circumspection and self-distrust. 
 
The absence of self-distrust is a certain sign of folly and approaching destruction.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:27
segments:
Hideth his eyes; from their wants. 
 
  Many a curse; from God and man.

entries.title: Proverbs 28:28
segments:
Rise; to power. 
 
  Men hide themselves; good men retire into obscurity, that they may avoid the persecution of the wicked.
